pr_body:
Adds a new mod that allows players to adjust the playback pitch of a song without affecting tempo.

The mod also provides a 'Match tempo' setting which will match the pitch to the songs tempo allowing users to effectively have double-time with a pitch adjustment. (I personally believe this is a better alternative to having local settings for each mod, open to others opinions on this however)

Only concern is that match tempo does not automatically update pitch at song select if tempo is changed after it is selected. This is because the match tempo pitch is done as a playfield update and not as a binding (since I couldn't figure out a way to avoid circular bindings) any feedback on this would be appreciated.

- [ ] Depends on [ppy/osu-framework#4118](https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/pull/4118)

Closes #9805 #9958
pr_comments:
> I personally believe this is a better alternative to having local settings for each mod, open to others opinions on this however

I'm not sure about this part. Users have [previously](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/9025) [complained](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11540) that the way daycore/nightcore is currently implemented sounds audibly worse with customised rates. This effectively makes it so that they have to use an entirely different mod for that purpose - and there are now two mods that change pitch, in different ways.

I think it would be better to have both pitch and rate as options on daycore/nightcore.
Why not just a checkbox on DT/HT as previously discussed? I think we already have enough mods that do almost the same thing, without adding more here.

> Why not just a checkbox on DT/HT as previously discussed?

My intention was to tackle a wider range of use cases then the single checkbox without having to introduce additional complexity. I did at first attempt what we discussed through DT/HT but the NC/DC implementations complicate it somewhat essentially requiring different implementations. I also thought it better to separate something that can be considered to have no performance advantage/disadvantage from the individual mod settings. And when ranked plays become a thing it seems simpler from a user's perspective that a mod would not affect rank-ability then an individual mod's setting. (if that is the route ranking was to go down)

> This effectively makes it so that they have to use an entirely different mod for that purpose

I agree somewhat, but I also think that having individual settings is almost just as bad from a user perspective.

> and there are now two mods that change pitch, in different ways.

While maybe not entirely relevant, the match tempo setting takes into account existing mod pitch adjustments for this purpose, when matching tempo, nightcore speed adjustments will correctly match pitch and tempo.

> While maybe not entirely relevant, the match tempo setting takes into account existing mod pitch adjustments for this purpose, when matching tempo, nightcore speed adjustments will correctly match pitch and tempo.

The problem I have with this is that now Double Time + Pitch Shift == Nightcore. That seems like a suboptimal setup.

The way I see it either Nightcore should be replaced with this mod (so you'd always use DT+PS - I shouldn't need to say that this is a *major* breaking change), or Nightcore should contain the pitch-controlling part wholly, without splitting out a separate mod for it.

> The problem I have with this is that now Double Time + Pitch Shift == Nightcore. That seems like a suboptimal setup.

Nightcore also includes beat samples but I understand your point. In a related manner, the timeramp mods already have the pitch adjust setting with default behaviour to adjust pitch. So if this mod is decided to be the direction to go in then there would need to be something to address timeramp which I admit is an issue(though probably not too complex).

Though I really think it best to avoid having several adjust pitch options for each mod. The settings list will quickly become cluttered when combining mods like DT and windup and should any other rate based mods ever get added the issue would only get worse. I admit that a lot of my arguments against stem from issues that could be _potentially_ come up in the future whether valid or not so I'd be willing to take a look into working into an alternative if that would be the agreed preferred direction (like per mod settings).

I highly doubt there will ever be more than two mods applied at the same time which adjust playback speed. Two is already going to get confusing from an implementation perspective (not sure if we *should* be allowed the example provided of WindUp + DoubleTime).

> not sure if we should be allowed the example provided of WindUp + DoubleTime

Current usage for DT + Windup is to set a base speedup with DT and then apply an additional ramp up speed. A change to Windup could easily replace that behaviour though in hindsight.

Just to keep things simple I still think this should be implemented in `ModRateAdjust` as a setting (which will be visible in all mods which derive from it, which are all the speed adjust ones). Probably with an exception for nightcore to have it *not* usable there (disable the bindable I guess?).

After reading through again, assuming wind-up eventually becomes incompatible with other rate mods then that would actually remove one of my bigger concerns with per-mod settings since only one pitch adjust setting would ever be visible to the user.

I'll work on the adjust pitch setting in ModRateAdjust then. Presumably would require a new separate PR?

issue_context.title: A mod who change the pitch but no the speed & Set pitch of the song according to DC/NC speed.
issue_context.body:
A mod with a 1.00x multiplier (he don't affects the score) when we can set the pitch of the song (between 0.5 and 2.0). But he don't affects the speed of the song too, like nightcore or wind up for exemple.

I have a 2nd idea, when we use Nightcore and Daycore mod, when we custom the speed of the song, we can add a optional 'adjust pitch' button where the pitch is modified according to the custom speed (for exemple, a song with NC mod with 1.3x increase speed is low pitched than the normal (1.5x)).
